author: karpathy
text: most common neural net mistakes: 1) you didn't try to overfit a single batch first. 2) you forgot to toggle train/eval mode for the net. 3) you forgot to .zero_grad() (in pytorch) before .backward(). 4) you passed softmaxed outputs to a loss that expects raw logits. ; others? :)

author: karpathy
text: @lishali88 I’ve used Software 2.0 to refer to the resulting artifact, the final piece of code, only portion of which is human designed. The act of writing it is a kind of fill in the blanks programming where you only write the general scaffolding.

author: karpathy
text: not a huge fan of the term "differentiable programming". The big deal isn't that it's differentiable, it's that there is any optimization over the code at all, instead of explicit code. I like/started to use "fill-in-the-blanks programming", artifacts of which are Software 2.0 :)
